If the fruit is an apple, then the Apples box must be Oranges and the Oranges box must be Apples. If the fruit is an orange, then the Apples box must be Apples & Oranges and the Oranges box must be Apples. This process of elimination ensures correct labeling.

The mislabeled 'Oranges' box can't be oranges (e1), so it must be the mixed box, leaving the remaining box correctly labeled by elimination.

Since every label is wrong, the box labelled Apples & Oranges cannot contain both fruits; it must contain only apples or only oranges. Sampling one fruit from this box tells us which single fruit it holds, fixing its true label. Knowing this, the remaining two boxes' labels can be deduced uniquely because their current labels are also incorrect. Hence we should take the fruit from the box labelled Apples & Oranges.
